newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris CEO opposes company split-up.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris CEO opposes company split-up.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos Inc chief executive Geoffrey Bible said on Thursday the tobacco and packaged goods giant would not be split up, even though top management had weighed such a proposal several years ago "It's something I personally would oppose enormously," Bible told a shareholder at the Philip Morris annual meeting.
"We acquired the food and beer companies to run them, not to spin them off," Bible said.

During questioning, a shareholder said Wall Street investors speculated that Philip Morris, a diversified group best known for its highly profitable cigarette businesses, would spin off some of its businesses.

The speculation has been driven recently by secret talks between tobacco companies and U.S. anti-tobacco forces aimed at a possible $300 billion or more resolution of court cases and public policy disputes.
Bible repeatedly declined during the meeting to comment on the secret talks, which began earlier this month.
